newsitem.title: JAPAN: Text of U.S. statement on US-Japan insurance pact.
newsitem.headline: Text of U.S. statement on US-Japan insurance pact.

text.p: The following is the text of the U.S. statement on Sunday announcing an agreement on opening Japan's insurance market, as issued by the U.S. embassy in Tokyo:

Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky and Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka reached final agreement today to resolve outstanding problems regarding the implementation of the 1994 U.S.-Japan insurance accord. Under the terms of the agreement, Japan will takes steps, consistent with the 1994 agreement, to dramatically deregulate the Japanese insurance market, the world's second largest with annual premiums of $341 billion but a foreign market share of only 3.58 percent. These new steps will allow foreign companies to compete more effectively and provide Japanese consumers with a greater choice of innovative products and lower prices.

Japan will take unprecedented action to introduce greater competition into the "primary sector" insurance market (predominantly life, auto, fire and other casualty insurance) that accounts for 95 percent of the Japanese insurance market. The government of Japan, for example, has committed to approve the introduction of auto insurance with variable premium rates, remove the rate-setting power of the "rating organizations," deregulate further the commercial fire insurance market, and streamline the introduction of new insurance products.

The government of Japan will also permit new subsidiaries to enter the "third sector" of the insurance market, but will provide for temporary measures that will prevent "radical change" in the business environment of that sector until after the primary sectors are deregulated. Those measures will assure greater competition in the Japanese market over time by allowing foreign and small insurance firms the ability to compete on a fair and equal basis.

Taken together, these measures represent fundamental changes in the Japanese insurance market, making it more open and competitive. The measures will present vastly expanded opportunities for both American and Japanese insurers and provide important benefits to Japanese consumers.
